posts.raw_content: And please pray for her husband Mike and their family. She passed on their anniversary. I'm sure Jesus is welcoming her and telling her "Well done, good and faithful servant." And I am happy for her that she is free. But it is a humongous loss for those of us here. Michelle was like an angel on earth, always there for others no matter what they were going through, she said she wanted to be God's hands and feet on earth. And she was. I met her bec she spotted my Trump hat at a concert so she came up to meet me and we became friends. A couple months later I went through a hard time and was home unwell and she and her husband were there with groceries, then with Christmas presents and elf costumes, and loving cheer. Michelle welcomed me into her family and into her heart. Despite her busy schedule I'd come home and find flowers at my door, and a card in my mailbox for every occasion. Michelle is special and made others feel special too. She was a beloved nanny, helping to raise many children over the years, and a companion helper to a lovely young woman with traumatic brain injury and an member of her TBI support group, as well a very active member of her own cancer support group. Her husband leads a project hero group for veterans and first responders, helping save lives from suicide. Mike also preaches God's word just in his own time live online twice a week, and has baptized many people. They both love the Lord and love people. To know them has been an immense privilege. They are two of God's finest people. And I know Michelle will be part of His Kingdom. I pray I get to see her again. I miss you my dearest Michellie 🤍💜
